chunks.text: CFG-5120 means the upstream connection pool exceeded its maximum size. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5120, raise pool.max_size or reduce concurrent callers. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-51200 means a TLS certificate is within its renewal window. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-51200, run the certificate renewal job. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-5102 means the request router found two rules with the same priority. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5102, give each routing rule a unique priority. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-5210 means the rate limiter lost contact with its counter store. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5210, restart the counter store client and replay the window. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-5121 means a plugin returned an invalid response header. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5121, disable the plugin and inspect its output. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-5112 means the health checker marked every node in a pool unhealthy. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5112, check network reachability from the probe nodes. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-5012 means the configured keepalive interval is below the minimum. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5012, restore the interval to at least 5 seconds. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-51020 means the access policy references a deleted role. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-51020, reassign the policy to an existing role. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-5201 means a canary stage exceeded its error budget. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5201, roll the canary back to stage zero. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-5220 means the DNS resolver returned an empty answer. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5220, verify the resolver address list. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-5122 means the audit sink rejected a batch of events. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5122, reduce the audit batch size. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-5110 means a websocket upgrade was denied by policy. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5110, review the websocket allow list. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-5021 means the compression module ran out of buffer space. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5021, increase the compression buffer. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-52100 means the session store reported a version mismatch. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-52100, flush the session store and reconnect. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-5111 means a retry budget was exhausted during a deployment. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5111, extend the retry budget for the rollout. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-5101 means the schema validator rejected a staged configuration. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5101, fix the schema errors reported in the diff. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-5212 means the metrics exporter could not bind its port. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5212, free the exporter port or change it. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-5202 means a backend returned more redirects than allowed. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5202, shorten the redirect chain at the backend. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-51210 means the request body exceeded the configured size limit. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-51210, raise body.max_bytes for the route. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-5120A means the leader election timed out. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5120A, restart the quorum members one at a time. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-5130 means an API key was presented from a blocked network. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5130, remove the address from the block list. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-5103 means the log shipper fell behind by more than a minute. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5103, scale out the log shipper workers. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-5230 means a route target resolved to a private address. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5230, point the route at a public target. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.
CFG-5113 means the failover controller found no standby region. The gateway logs it as a warning for the control plane.
To recover from CFG-5113, register a standby region before enabling failover. Reload the gateway configuration afterwards.

Incident INC-7001 affected the auth service. The symptom was failed health probes.
The root cause of INC-7001 was a saturated log shipper. The fix was to scale the shippers.
Incident INC-7002 affected the billing service. The symptom was slow report generation.
The root cause of INC-7002 was a clock skew between nodes. The fix was to resync the node clocks.
Incident INC-7003 affected the ledger service. The symptom was intermittent 502 responses.
The root cause of INC-7003 was an expired intermediate certificate. The fix was to renew the certificate chain.
Incident INC-7004 affected the search service. The symptom was high memory usage.
The root cause of INC-7004 was a leaked connection pool. The fix was to restart the pool owner.
Incident INC-7005 affected the notify service. The symptom was slow login pages.
The root cause of INC-7005 was a misconfigured keepalive interval. The fix was to set the interval to 10 seconds.
Incident INC-7006 affected the report service. The symptom was login redirect loops.
The root cause of INC-7006 was a wrong redirect target. The fix was to correct the redirect URL.
Incident INC-7007 affected the export service. The symptom was stuck deployments.
The root cause of INC-7007 was a disabled compression module. The fix was to enable compression.
Incident INC-7008 affected the import service. The symptom was missing audit entries.
The root cause of INC-7008 was a counter store failover. The fix was to restart the counter client.
Incident INC-7009 affected the audit service. The symptom was dropped websocket sessions.
The root cause of INC-7009 was a plugin that blocked the event loop. The fix was to disable the plugin.
Incident INC-7010 affected the cache service. The symptom was timeouts on import jobs.
The root cause of INC-7010 was an outdated schema version. The fix was to migrate the schema.
Incident INC-7011 affected the auth service. The symptom was unavailable status page.
The root cause of INC-7011 was a paused canary stage. The fix was to resume the canary.
Incident INC-7012 affected the billing service. The symptom was missing request logs.
The root cause of INC-7012 was a mistyped route target. The fix was to correct the route.
Incident INC-7013 affected the ledger service. The symptom was failed nightly exports.
The root cause of INC-7013 was a full disk on the log node. The fix was to expand the log volume.
Incident INC-7014 affected the search service. The symptom was unexpected 404 responses.
The root cause of INC-7014 was a throttled API key. The fix was to raise the key limit.
Incident INC-7015 affected the notify service. The symptom was queue backlog growth.
The root cause of INC-7015 was a lost standby registration. The fix was to register the standby.
Incident INC-7016 affected the report service. The symptom was duplicate notifications.
The root cause of INC-7016 was two rules sharing one priority. The fix was to assign unique priorities.
Incident INC-7017 affected the export service. The symptom was delayed invoices.
The root cause of INC-7017 was an exhausted retry budget. The fix was to extend the budget.
Incident INC-7018 affected the import service. The symptom was stale search results.
The root cause of INC-7018 was a stale DNS cache entry. The fix was to flush the DNS cache.
Incident INC-7019 affected the audit service. The symptom was certificate warnings.
The root cause of INC-7019 was an oversized request header. The fix was to raise the header limit.
Incident INC-7020 affected the cache service. The symptom was failed configuration reloads.
The root cause of INC-7020 was an unreleased leader lock. The fix was to release the lock manually.
Incident INC-7021 affected the auth service. The symptom was empty metrics dashboards.
The root cause of INC-7021 was a missing index on the ticket table. The fix was to add the missing index.
Incident INC-7022 affected the billing service. The symptom was inconsistent rate limits.
The root cause of INC-7022 was a session store mismatch. The fix was to flush the session store.
Incident INC-7023 affected the ledger service. The symptom was slow DNS lookups.
The root cause of INC-7023 was a broken health probe path. The fix was to fix the probe path.
Incident INC-7024 affected the search service. The symptom was rejected uploads.
The root cause of INC-7024 was a blocked exporter port. The fix was to free the exporter port.
